dialogues.speaker: Devitt
dialogues.text: Interested in this tale, are you? Hahaha. I'll go over it with you — it's not too long a tale.

dialogues.speaker: Devitt
dialogues.text: Hmm... So our tale begins with a masterful hatter.

dialogues.speaker: Devitt
dialogues.text: This maker of hats made the very best ones in the world, and each day, there would be a stupendous crowd outside his door. Still, he would make each hat properly and beautifully.

dialogues.speaker: Devitt
dialogues.text: Some said that he had even once been commissioned by a goddess to make ten beautiful hats of different styles.

dialogues.speaker: Devitt
dialogues.text: To thank him for his craftsmanship, she offered to grant him a wish. But the hatmaker said that he did not have any unfulfilled wishes.

dialogues.speaker: Devitt
dialogues.text: He loved what he did, making hats, and everyone loved the hats he made — and that was enough for him.

dialogues.speaker: Devitt
dialogues.text: The goddess acknowledged his noble answer, but also stated that her promise would remain valid.

dialogues.speaker: Devitt
dialogues.text: Should he ever be willing to make a wish, she would be ready to grant it immediately.
